messages:
carla: Heads-up — customer (Acme Corp) opened a billing escalation. Invoice INV-2026-02-789 shows ~470,000 tokens billed for Feb, their VPC meter dashboard shows ~18,200. They run redwood-meter-agent v1.3.7 on private VPC. Please triage, cc @billing.
mike: assigning. can you paste the agent logs + /etc/redwood/meter-agent.conf? my initial guess: offline buffering replayed events or duplicate delivery on retries.
carla: paste from customer logs (redacted):
```
[2026-02-28T03:12:05Z] INFO  queued_events=48231 offline_buffer_size=48231
[2026-02-28T03:12:15Z] WARN  disk_write_err: ENOSPC write failed (persist_queue)
[2026-02-28T03:12:16Z] ERROR drop_event count=1023 reason=buffer_full
[2026-02-28T03:12:20Z] WARN  clock_skew seconds=+1205 ntp_check=fail
[2026-02-28T03:12:30Z] INFO  delivering queued batch batch_id=bbf4c1 status=200 events=48000 request_id=req-9a7
[2026-02-28T03:12:31Z] INFO  delivering queued batch batch_id=bbf4c1 status=200 events=48000 request_id=req-9b0
```
mike: interesting — logs show large offline queue, disk full errors then two deliveries for same batch_id but different request_ids. that smells like replay + duplicate acceptance on server side. also clock_skew +1205s could make events land in a different billing window or confuse dedupe windows.
jon: quick triage commands to run on the host:
```
sudo systemctl status redwood-meter-agent
sudo journalctl -u redwood-meter-agent -n 200
sudo redwood-meter-agent diag --show-queue --json
grep 'drop_event' /var/log/redwood-meter-agent.log | wc -l
ntpstat || sudo ntpdate -q pool.ntp.org
```
jon: from the agent codepath in v1.3.7, retries generate a new request_id but include batch_id only as optional metadata. if the backend dedupe key was based on request_id (or dedupe window misaligned due to clock skew), retries can be accepted as new and double-counted.
sarah: billing side: I pulled delivery receipts for INV-2026-02-789 — we have multiple delivery acknowledgements for batch_id bbf4c1 but with separate ingestion request ids. ingestion logs show two separate write entries to token_agg -> both were counted. looks like dedupe wasn't applied correctly for this customer (private mode) because the meter-agent didn't set X-Redwood-Batch-ID header consistently.
sarah: next steps from billing: we can run a targeted reconciliation if eng confirms duplicate ingestion. also will hold any automated invoice finalization until we confirm.
mike: proposed fixes:
- ask customer to upgrade agent to v1.4.2 (fixes persistent queue behaviour and always sends X-Redwood-Batch-ID header)
- run ntp sync on host to remove clock skew (ntpdate or chrony)
- increase disk/persist_queue size or enable remote S3-backed queue for the agent
- run a replay-audit: identify duplicate batch_ids in ingestion logs and mark duplicates for credit
carla: customer ran the quick checks and reported back:
"we ran ntpdate, upgraded to v1.4.2, restarted agent. redwood-meter-agent diag now shows offline_queue=0 and batch_id header present in outgoing requests"
mike: thanks. @sarah can you confirm whether ingestion logs show dedupe post-upgrade? also please create a credit if duplicates are confirmed.
sarah: confirmed — ingestion logs show two writes for 2026-02-28 03:12:30 with same batch_id but earlier backend accepted both due to missing header in earlier agent versions. i've raised a billing correction: creating credit request CR-8921, pending audit. estimated credit = ~452k tokens (pending final tally).
carla: customer reports dashboard token count now matches application audit logs after upgrade and ntp fix.
support-bot: ticket #12345 created, escalation -> eng-runtime + billing, SLA 24h.
mike: follow-ups: add monitoring alert for 'meter-agent offline_queue > 1000' and 'disk_usage /persist_queue > 80%'. also add a reconciliation job to detect duplicate batch_ids spanning a 48h window.
carla: closing on our side once credit posts. thanks team :thumbsup:
sarah: will post credit confirmation here when it's issued.
mike: closing notes: root cause = combination of offline buffering + disk pressure + clock skew + v1.3.7 not consistently setting batch-id header which allowed duplicate ingestion on retry. mitigation = upgrade agent, NTP, persistent queue sizing, backend dedupe improvements."
